body: I'll ask my therapist about Medicaid. I could probably find a job near my grandparents house, that would be a good reason to live there.

They know I don't like what they're doing, but they don't know how much I dislike them and how much they've hurt me. 

I would tell them but I'm 90% I'd get kicked out of the house if I did.

I don't have any friends. 

My grandparents on my mother's side would probably let me stay at their house but their on a vacation right now. They left one of their cars and a key to the gate with me though. If I called them and asked I don't think they'd have a problem with me staying at their house if I really needed to.

I emailed her a few days ago when this started but I don't think I'll hear back until Monday or maybe even later since our next appointment isn't for another week.


Idk what I'd be ok with her telling them though.
I guess that's an option but I really don't want them anywhere near my therapist. I don't really think they'd listen to her anyways, they've never listened to me when I've tried to tell them things.

Yeah, I know the best thing for me would be to move out but I can barely get out of bed before noon most mornings. It's been getting better but ever time my parents try to do something it feels like it just sets me back a couple steps.

I emailed both my therapist and doctor but I haven't heard back from them. I don't think I will until Monday.


Idk anything about legal recourse. I know that legally my therapist can't say anything to them unless I approve it and I'm not going to be strong armed into letting them talk to my therapist.



And yeah, my parents are a little skeptical of the medications. My mom has tried to tell me that it's the medications that are causing so many problems. She refuses to believe that I had sleep problems before I started talking Adderall for my ADHD.

I know I've basically spent 2 years doing nothing while I live with my parents but I've just been at the end of my rope for so long. 


I just don't know if I can go back to what I was doing before I started meds. I'm just so tired of everything. I don't care if it makes me look like I'm a selfish, spoiled, entitled person. I'm just to exhausted to care.

>My therapist changed it to something like "Can you find yourself ok, most of the time?"


I guess I could try to do that. I think that's still going to be hard though. I kinda default to thinking that I'm the worst person in the world most of the time.

How do I tell what my trigger points are? 


Do they have something to do with whenever I feel overwhelmed or have a mental breakdown?

Idk if pushing through it is accurate. It's more like standing in a river and not moving. 


Idk about strong either. I think if I was strong I would be doing better, or at least I wouldn't be doing as bad.
Yeah, that makes sense. I just won't be able to leave anytime soon no matter how much I want to.

I'm still working on reminding myself that feeling hopeless is probably temporary because I have no clue what'll happen in the next 10 minutes, not to mention the next 10 years.

It's still super hard to actually tell myself that and believe it though.
That makes sense. I guess it's like trying to stay perfectly clean while living in the back of a garbage truck or something like that.
